subject: ai
question: Explain Alpha-Beta Pruning and show how it improves Minimax.
title: Alpha-Beta: Skip the Useless
hook: What if a game AI could skip most of its thinking?
answer: Minimax: MAX picks the highest child value, MIN the lowest; every leaf is evaluated (example tree: MIN nodes 3, 2, 2, root = 3, all 9 leaves checked)
Alpha-beta pruning gives the same result as minimax but skips branches that cannot change it
Alpha = best value MAX is already guaranteed (starts at minus infinity); beta = best value MIN is already guaranteed (starts at plus infinity)

Prune a branch when alpha >= beta. Example: first MIN node gives 3, so alpha = 3; second MIN node sees 2 first, so beta <= 2 < alpha and its remaining leaves 4 and 6 are pruned; third node searched fully; answer still 3
Improvement: same best move with fewer nodes; with good move ordering it can search about twice as deep in the same time
Memory trick: alpha is MAX's floor, beta is MIN's ceiling
